title: Fair Work Amendment (Protecting Weekend Pay and Penalty Rates) Bill 2017
short_title: Fair Work Amendment (Protecting Weekend Pay and Penalty Rates) Bill 2017

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would prevent modern award penalty rates being reduced below their level on 1 January 2017 by imposing a statutory floor on award variations.
It would make Fair Work Commission determinations ineffective where they cut a modern award's penalty rates beneath that benchmark, including the February 2017 decision.
The amendments would begin on Royal Assent and apply to commission determinations varying modern award penalty rates made on or after 22 January 2017.
changes: A new section would prohibit award variations that reduced penalty rates below the benchmark.
Determinations breaching the protected rate would have no legal effect.
The application rule would cover determinations already made since the specified January date.
summary.affected: Employees and employers covered by modern awards containing penalty rates, and the Fair Work Commission, are affected.

speeches.speaker: Adam Bandt
speeches.brief: The Greens introduced the Fair Work Amendment (Protecting Weekend Pay and Penalty Rates) Bill 2017 to block the Fair Work Commission’s penalty rate cuts for young and low-paid workers, arguing weekend and public holiday rates are essential for living wages. The bill would prevent rates from falling below their start-of-2017 levels, and the Greens challenged Senators Hinch, Xenophon and Hanson to support it.
